To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the processing of emotional expressions and of gaze direction interact rather late and complexly to modulate spatial selective attention.

(a) the GOE is enhanced by emotional faces compared to neutral ones; (b) the GOE for emotional faces is modulated by the type of emotion expressed; (c) the ERP modulation of the GOE is different for different emotions; and (d) the ERP modulation is different for different components of the GOE.

(i) the processing of social information, such as gaze and emotional expressions, interacts in a complex manner with the orienting of visual attention; (ii) the orienting of attention to the location indicated by the gaze is modulated by the emotion expressed in the face; (iii) these effects are observed in non-anxious healthy participants; (iv) they are not related to early attention-related ERP components (EDAN and ADAN); and (v) they affect both behavioral and ERP
In summary, our research is concerned with
the impact of emotional expressions of the human face on the orienting of visual attention.
the role of emotion and attention in the processing of social stimuli.
the impact of emotional facial expressions on gaze-oriented attention, which is a crucial process in social interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the processing of facial emotion and gaze direction interact in a complex manner, and that this interaction is modulated by the type of emotion expressed.
the processing of emotional facial expressions and gaze orientation are both involved in the modulation of spatial attention, with the latter being more efficient than the former.
emotions modulate attention in a late and complex manner, but that they also modulate the processing of gaze cues in a late manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
gaze and facial expressions interact at different stages in the processing of visual stimuli.
the processing of emotional facial expressions is not only modulated by gaze, but also modulates gaze processing.

the emotional content of the face is not processed at the same time as gaze direction and that the processing of gaze and emotions is not additive but rather interactive, with emotions modulating gaze processing and gaze modulating emotional processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
emotions influence gaze-oriented attention.
emotions and gaze interact in modulating spatial attention.
the processing of emotional faces and the processing of gaze are not independent, but they interact at several processing stages.
